title: Strict transform on the preserved open
statement:
Let $f\colon Y\to X$, let $\mathcal I$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent
ideal, and put $X'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$. Over
$U=X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$, the strict transform is canonically
$Y\times_XU$, and its map to $Y$ is the ordinary pullback isomorphism.

proof.text:
The blow-up is the identity over $U$ by
[thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement]. Under this specified
isomorphism the open whose closure defines the strict transform is all of
$Y\times_XU$. It is already a closed subscheme of itself, so the minimal
closed-subscheme characterization of
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-closure-characterization] identifies
the restriction with $Y\times_XU$. On charts this is the quotient by the
zero torsion ideal after $a$ is inverted; these identifications agree on
overlaps by the closed chart model in
[prop-nagata-strict-transform-closed-fiber-product]. The projection
equality is the one induced by the fibre-product square.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f\colon Y\to X$ and $\pi\colon X'\to X$ be morphisms and let
$U\subseteq X$ be an open subscheme over which $\pi$ is an isomorphism,
$\pi^{-1}(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ (for instance
$X'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ and $U=X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$).
Let $\Omega\subseteq Y\times_XX'$ be the open subscheme lying over $U$, as in
[def-nagata-strict-transform].
Then $\Omega$, together with its projection to $Y$ and the map
$\Omega\to\pi^{-1}(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}U$, is a fibre product of $f$ and the
inclusion $U\hookrightarrow X$; that is, $\Omega\cong Y\times_XU$
compatibly with the projections to $Y$.

proof.text:
Write $p_1\colon Y\times_XX'\to Y$ and $p_2\colon Y\times_XX'\to X'$ for
the projections. By definition $\Omega=p_2^{-1}(\pi^{-1}(U))$. Restricting
a morphism to the preimage of an open gives a fibre square, so $\Omega$
with the restriction $p_2|_\Omega\colon\Omega\to\pi^{-1}(U)$ is a fibre
product of $p_2$ and the open immersion $\pi^{-1}(U)\hookrightarrow X'$.
Pasting this square with the fibre square defining $Y\times_XX'$ shows that
$\Omega$, with $p_1|_\Omega$ and $p_2|_\Omega$, is a fibre product of $f$
and the composite $\pi^{-1}(U)\hookrightarrow X'\to X$, which is
$\pi^{-1}(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}U\hookrightarrow X$. Replacing
$\pi^{-1}(U)$ by $U$ along the isomorphism $\pi|_{\pi^{-1}(U)}$ gives the
asserted fibre square.
